title: Compare two functions: the start and the step

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A taxi ride costs three dollars to get in, plus two dollars for each mile.

do.text: A taxi costs $\cg{3}$ dollars to get in, plus $\cw{2}$ dollars for each mile.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: As a table, x is the miles and y the dollars: zero, three. One, five. Two, seven. Three, nine.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: As a graph, each row is a point.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The points fall on one straight line.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: As an equation: y equals two x, plus three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each form holds the same two numbers. The start: three dollars, at zero miles.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: It is the initial value, or y-intercept: where the line meets the y-axis.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The step: two dollars more for every mile. It is the rate of change, or slope.

do.text: $\cw{\text{Step}}$: the rate of change, for each 1 of $x$.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Any form: find the start, find the step.

do.text: Any form: find the start, find the step.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Function A is given by the table. Function B is given by the graph. Which has the greater rate of change? Which has the greater initial value?

do.text: Function A is given by the table. Function B is given by the graph. Which has the greater rate of change? Which has the greater initial value?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Find the start and the step of each.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: In the table, x goes up two each row, and y goes up four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four for every two is two for every one. A's step is two.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So A starts at three?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Only if x were zero. Here x is one. Walk back one step: three, minus two, is one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Graph B meets the y-axis at twelve. That is its start.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: It falls to zero at x equals four: down twelve in four steps of one. Its step is negative three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now put A on the same graph. Each row is a point, and the line runs back to its start.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: B is steeper. So B has the greater rate of change?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Steeper, but falling. A climbs two each step, and B falls three. Two is greater than negative three.

do.text: A falling line has a negative step, however steep.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And B starts higher: twelve is greater than one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: So A has the greater rate of change, and B has the greater initial value.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A rate can be a speed. Car A is shown in the table. Car B travels two hundred eighty miles in five hours. Which car is faster, and by how many miles per hour?

do.text: Car A is shown in the table. Car B travels 280 miles in 5 hours. Which car is faster, and by how many miles per hour?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Both cars start at zero, so the step is miles divided by hours. Car A: eighty miles in two hours, forty miles per hour.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Car B: two hundred eighty divided by five is fifty-six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Fifty-six minus forty is sixteen. Car B, by sixteen miles per hour.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: But after five hours, B is eighty miles ahead.

do.text: After 5 hours, B is $80$ miles ahead.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Sixteen more miles each hour, for five hours, is eighty. The speeds differ by sixteen.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Last, is a function linear at all? Which equation defines a function that is not linear?

do.text: Which equation defines a function that is not linear?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Linear means the same step every time, so the graph is a straight line.

do.text: Linear: the same step every time.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: I'll try x squared plus two. At x equals one, two and three: three, six, eleven.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The steps are three, then five. Not the same!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The straight line through the first two points misses the third.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So y equals x squared plus two is not linear.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The others fit y equals m x plus b. Four times x plus five is four x plus twenty.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And y equals three is zero x plus three: a step of zero every time, so it is linear too.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: In any form, find the step: the change in y for each one of x.

do.text: $\cw{\text{Step}}$: the change in $y$ for each 1 of $x$.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Find the start: y when x is zero. If it is hidden, walk back.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Compare them as numbers, signs and all.

do.text: Compare them as numbers, signs and all.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Linear means the same step every time.

do.text: Linear: the same step every time.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Any form: find the start, find the step.

do.text: Any form: find the start, find the step.
